definition: Rendering a scene from camera viewpoints never captured, using methods like NeRF and 3D Gaussian splatting that learn an implicit scene representation.
details: Rendering a scene from camera viewpoints never captured, using methods like NeRF and 3D Gaussian splatting that learn an implicit scene representation.

explainer.lead: Novel view synthesis renders a scene from camera viewpoints that were never captured. It matters because it lets systems generate new perspectives of a scene from existing imagery.

tiers.eli5: It is like walking around a photograph and seeing what the scene would look like from the side, even though no one took a picture from there.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use methods like NeRF and 3D Gaussian splatting, which learn an implicit scene representation from captured views. A consideration is that the rendering depends on that learned representation rather than on direct captures.
tiers.paperLevel: Rendering a scene from camera viewpoints never captured, using methods such as NeRF and 3D Gaussian splatting that learn an implicit scene representation.

explainer.example: Given a set of photos of an object, a NeRF representation is learned and then rendered from an angle that was not among the original photos.
